common_name: Inticancha Series Alstroemeria (Non-Stop-Blooming Compact Patio Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Set tubers about eight inches deep in spring into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Inticancha is a compact, exceptionally floriferous Peruvian lily series bred by Konst Breeding for patio containers and small garden beds.

directions: Set tubers about eight inches deep in spring into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, handling the brittle roots carefully during planting. Inticancha is a Peruvian lily series bred by the Dutch firm Konst Breeding, the same house behind the Colorita and Princess Lily lines, selected for an unusually dense, continuous flush of funnel-shaped flowers across a wide color range from soft whites and pastel pinks through vivid orange, red, and purple bicolors, carried over a compact, well-branched mound of narrow foliage. Like its sister series, Inticancha is self-cleaning, dropping spent blooms without deadheading, and flowers repeatedly from late spring into fall without the vernalization period some older alstroemeria types need for rebloom. Its low, tidy habit was bred specifically for patio pots, hanging baskets, and small border fronts where taller cut-flower alstroemeria would be out of scale. Pull rather than cut spent flower stems from the base to stimulate further flushes, mulch heavily for winter protection at the colder end of its hardiness range, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring if flowering declines.
sources: Konst Breeding B.V. — Inticancha Alstroemeria product literature
